heading: Three observational CLI checks
introduction: These commands are documented for FortiOS 7.4.7. Use your authorized FortiGate CLI console or approved SSH session, in the correct administrative context. A CLI is a text interface: type one complete command at its prompt and inspect the result before continuing. Consult the matching reference if your version or permissions differ; stop on an unsupported-command error. These checks were not executed against the customer's system or a lab for this article.
privacyNote: Output can expose endpoint identifiers, addresses, posture information and policy names. Keep it in an approved private record and sanitize it before sharing. Large listings can be verbose; prefer the relevant GUI view when you do not need a full listing. These are observation commands, not access-granting configuration changes.

checks.observation: Identify the expected EMS and its reported connection state. The FortiClient NAC daemon (fcnacd) manages this connectivity.
checks.limit: This does not establish that a specific endpoint is authorized or that PAM is reachable.

checks.purpose: Inspect dynamic address information associated with EMS posture tags.
checks.observation: Compare the relevant tag and address entries with the endpoint and policy under investigation. Correlate identity separately, especially when addresses are shared or translated.
checks.limit: A listed address or tag alone is not proof that the complete policy matched the test request.

checks.purpose: Inspect statistics associated with application-gateway rules.
checks.observation: WAD is the FortiGate process handling proxy work. Compare relevant statistics before and after the timestamped test, alongside the request logs.
checks.limit: A counter can include unrelated traffic. It does not independently prove backend delivery or successful application login.
